beginner.headline: Today (Wed Oct 14): conditional for beginners. Canoes 2–3 ft, thigh to waist (Surfline), but 13 s SSW sets can run chest to shoulder, occasionally head-high. ENE trades light early (7 kt, gusts 16 kt reported), up to 15 kt later. Best 7–10 AM, falling from the 6:23 AM high (2.1 ft).
beginner.recommendation: Plan for 7–10 AM: the tide falls from the 6:23 AM high (2.1 ft) toward the 1:47 PM low (0.6 ft), so the reef has the most water early, and trades are lightest early (Surfline 7 kt ENE with gusts to 16 kt; NWS ENE up to 15 kt today). Watch several full set cycles before starting: the average is thigh to waist, but the forecaster reports chest-to-shoulder sets and occasional head-high ones on the 13 s SSW swell, and those reach further inside. Gusts are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift on gusts. The DOH list was not read, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if sets stay small inside and drift is low. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.why: The eha-cloud live list could not be fetched this run (fourth run in a row); the DOH CWB announcement page only points to it. News searches found no new Waikīkī or Oʻahu notice in October (Kauaʻi brown-water advisories were reported Sep 30 and Oct 3; current status not verified). Dry, stable weather (NWS) lowers runoff risk but proves nothing.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; coastal water usually needs about 48 hours to flush.
